AdultAccountOut.description:
Create My Account (story 1.6): the adult sign-up, with the first name, date of birth and
email filled in from the teen account. The email and date of birth can't change.

AffectedTeen.title: AffectedTeen
AffectedTeen.description: An invited teen whose account and data go with an Account Deletion.

AnswerContentRef.title: AnswerContentRef
AnswerContentRef.description:
The gap's answer: an Admin's waiting for approval, the published one, or an Admin's
rejected one, with the Super Admin's reason (6.3: back to New, with the reason on the
answer).

AnswerIn.title: AnswerIn
AnswerIn.description:
One answer, in the form its question's kind takes (app/health/values.py). `other` is the
write-in, for the choice that takes one.

AppointmentIn.title: AppointmentIn

AuditActor.title: AuditActor
AuditActor.description: Who: their name and role. Null id and name for the system or someone not signed in.

AuditFilters.title: AuditFilters
AuditFilters.description:
10.1's Search and Filter. Dates are times with a time zone (the panel sends the start and
end of the admin's chosen days); a time without one is taken as UTC. Both ends included.

AuditTarget.title: AuditTarget
AuditTarget.description:
What it affected: a type (user, admin_invitation, support_request...) and id, with a
name for accounts and Admin invites.

ChangePlan.title: ChangePlan
ChangePlan.description:
Individual to Family applies at once and needs the new monthly total confirmed (checked
by the service); Family to Individual applies from the next billing date.

ChooseSafetyOption.title: ChooseSafetyOption
ChooseSafetyOption.description:
Story 3.2: the option the client picked on the emergency or crisis screen: "Iâve called
for help" (`called_for_help`, emergency) or "Iâve reached out for help" (`reached_out`,
crisis), or "Iâm safe now" (`safe_now`). It's saved as the client's next message, so
`client_msg_id` works as it does for any message.

CircleMapOut.title: CircleMapOut
CircleMapOut.description:
Story 6.1's Hypothalamus Circle Map: Deborah's predefined map with the profile's
symptoms highlighted. The map's areas and symptoms are a placeholder until Deborah's map is
in (`placeholder` true; app/health/circle_map.json).

CompleteHealthProfileWidget.title: CompleteHealthProfileWidget
CompleteHealthProfileWidget.description: Shown until the health profile is complete. Complete now opens My Health's form.

ConfirmationsOut.title: ConfirmationsOut
ConfirmationsOut.description: The stories' confirmation texts, filled in for this client.

ConsultWidget.title: ConsultWidget
ConsultWidget.description:
Consult with support team: opens 10.1's consultation form (POST
/profiles/{profile_id}/support-requests with kind "consultation"). Not on a teen's own
account.

ContentEdit.title: ContentEdit
ContentEdit.description: 6.1's Edit: the title, content type and text (or file).

ContentNew.title: ContentNew
ContentNew.description:
6.2's Add Content form. `knowledge_gap_id` is set when it's added from a gap's Add
answer (6.3).

ConversationSummary.title: ConversationSummary
ConversationSummary.description: A row in the conversation list: "Waking at 3am Â· 3 days ago".

ConversationWidget.title: ConversationWidget
ConversationWidget.description: Continue your conversation, or Ask the Oracle when there's none yet (always shown).

CreateProviderNotes.title: CreateProviderNotes
CreateProviderNotes.description:
Create my notes (story 3.4). The app makes `client_request_id` once and sends it again
with any retry, so the notes are never made twice.

`booking` is the answer to "Have you booked an appointment with a provider?":
- "booked": the card (filled in from what the client mentioned, in Scenario A);
- "not_yet": the specialty the Oracle suggested (its appointment card widget), with no
  provider or date;
- "skip": no details; the notes are for a primary care provider.

CreateTeenDeletionBody.title: CreateTeenDeletionBody
CreateTeenDeletionBody.description: + Create deletion request, for a teen who can't sign in at all and emailed the team.

CreateVisitLog.title: CreateVisitLog
CreateVisitLog.description:
A new log. `provider_notes_id` links it to a set of provider-ready notes (Log visit on a
note card, or the post-visit notification); without it, it's a standalone visit (+ Log a
visit). The app makes `client_request_id` once and sends it again with any retry, so the
visit is never logged twice.

DeletionNoticeOut.title: DeletionNoticeOut
DeletionNoticeOut.description: What the app shows during a grace period (stories 1.2, 8.2 and 11.4).

DeletionRequestBody.title: DeletionRequestBody
DeletionRequestBody.description: Story 8.2: the client types the family member's first name to confirm.

DraftBody.title: DraftBody
DraftBody.description:
Saving a draft: the fields sent replace what's there. Either may be empty until it's
published.

EditAdminIn.title: EditAdminIn
EditAdminIn.description:
7.1's Edit: first and last name. The email can be sent unchanged (the panel may send
the whole form), but can't be changed.

EmailChangeRequestBody.title: EmailChangeRequestBody
EmailChangeRequestBody.description:
Story 11.1's Request email change. The app makes `client_request_id` once per request
and sends it again with any retry, so the request reaches the team once.

EscalationProfile.title: EscalationProfile
EscalationProfile.description: Who it's about: the client, a family member (with the advocate's name), or a teen.

FamilyMemberName.title: FamilyMemberName
FamilyMemberName.description: A managed family member, for the Delete Account disclaimer's list of everyone affected.

FamilyOverview.title: FamilyOverview
FamilyOverview.description:
The Manage Family screen: "2 of 3 active family members" and a card for each member,
turned-off ones included. Unfinished drafts aren't listed; Add family member resumes one.
Invited teens have their own cards, with no health information (8.2), and count towards the
places from the invite (8.1).

GiveFeedback.title: GiveFeedback
GiveFeedback.description:
A thumbs up or down on one of the Oracle's replies, with an optional comment. Giving
it again replaces the earlier one.

HealthFactOut.title: HealthFactOut
HealthFactOut.description:
A change a logged visit suggests (story 5.2: "the Oracle asks the Client before updating
their health profile"), for the client to confirm, edit or discard. Details from
conversations aren't facts: they're saved straight away (3.1, 6 Nov 19:22).

HealthProfileEdit.title: HealthProfileEdit
HealthProfileEdit.description:
A save in My Health: one section's Edit, or a step of Complete my profile.

- `answers`: question key -> the new answer, or null to remove it (6.1: optional and
  sensitive answers "can be edited or deleted at any time"). An empty text also removes.
  Answers that depend on each other can be sent together: each question is checked with
  the answers before it in this same save.
- `remove_sections`: removes every saved answer in these sections, including answers kept
  from questions that no longer apply (for example "body_follow_ups").
- Nothing is saved if any part is refused.

HealthProfileView.title: HealthProfileView
HealthProfileView.description:
3.1's health profile, read-only: the client's own profile (a teen's too), as My Health
shows it, without what's only for editing (no editable fields, suggested answers, or the
conversation an answer came from). Health data.

HomeDashboardOut.title: HomeDashboardOut
HomeDashboardOut.description: The active profile's Home Dashboard. `widgets` are in the story's order.

IntakeAnswers.title: IntakeAnswers
IntakeAnswers.description:
The answer to one intake step. Send only that step's fields. The Back button changes
an earlier answer by sending it again. Family-only fields are refused on the client's own
profile, and so is a date of birth different from sign-up's.

InvitationOut.title: InvitationOut
InvitationOut.description: The setup screen: the name and email from the invite, filled in and locked.

InvitedTeenCard.title: InvitedTeenCard
InvitedTeenCard.description:
An invited teen with their own account, as the parent entered them, and the status.
Never anything of the teen's own.

KnowledgeScreen.title: KnowledgeScreen
KnowledgeScreen.description:
6.1's Knowledge Base screen: the number of new gaps (and content waiting for approval).
The listing is GET /admin/knowledge/contents.

LabIn.title: LabIn
LabIn.description:
A row of "Labs ordered". A lab the notes requested that the provider didn't order is
sent with `ordered` false (5.2: "the Client leaves them unmarked"). Rows with no name are
left out.

LibraryOut.title: LibraryOut
LibraryOut.description:
The Wellness Protocols library as this profile sees it: teens and children get no
product tabs, shop links or cleanse protocols. A tab with nothing published isn't listed.

LibrarySectionOut.title: LibrarySectionOut
LibrarySectionOut.description:
A section with published knowledge base content (Super Admin 6.1): only those are
listed, so an archived protocol disappears and an edit shows straight away.

LinkOut.title: LinkOut
LinkOut.description: A link into the Wellness Protocols library: opens `tab` at `section`.

MeOut.title: MeOut

MedicineChangeIn.title: MedicineChangeIn
MedicineChangeIn.description: A row of "Changes in prescriptions or supplements". Rows with no name are left out.

MyFamilyWidget.title: MyFamilyWidget
MyFamilyWidget.description:
The Family plan's family profiles and invited teens, with Add family member. On the
trial or the Individual plan it's locked: the Family plan's upgrade prompt. Hidden while a
family member's profile is active, and on a teen's own account.

MyHealthWidget.title: MyHealthWidget
MyHealthWidget.description: Quick access to My Health (6.1). Always shown.

MyProfileEdit.title: MyProfileEdit
MyProfileEdit.description:
Edit: the first name, the state and the ZIP code can change. The other fields on the
screen may be sent back unchanged, so the app can send the whole form; a different email,
date of birth or country is refused. `confirm_teen_rules` is the client's Confirm on the
teen rules message, sent again with the same state.

MyProfileOut.title: MyProfileOut
MyProfileOut.description:
The Profile & Account screen's account details: no phone number, and the ZIP code is
back in the 6 Nov stories.

NeedsAttention.title: NeedsAttention
NeedsAttention.description: What's open now, whatever the date range.

NextStep.title: NextStep

NextStepIn.title: NextStepIn
NextStepIn.description: A row of "Next steps". Rows with no text are left out.

NotesCard.title: NotesCard
NotesCard.description: A set of notes in a list (the conversation's, or the profile's for My Visit Notes).

NotesHeaderOut.title: NotesHeaderOut
NotesHeaderOut.description:
The notes' header (story 3.4), filled in by the backend: the first name only, the date
of birth (the Oracle never gets it), and the appointment details that are known.

NotesResult.title: NotesResult

NotesText.title: NotesText
NotesText.description:
Copy text (story 3.5): the full notes as plain text, with the disclaimer and, when
relevant, the disclosure box.

NoticeOut.title: NoticeOut

PaymentMethodLink.title: PaymentMethodLink
PaymentMethodLink.description:
The provider's page for changing the payment method. When the client comes back, the
app shows 11.3's "Your payment method has been updated.".

PillarOut.title: PillarOut
PillarOut.description:
One of the Five Pillars, opened from the accordion: the personal adjustment and the
library links (See the protocol).

PlanCardOut.title: PlanCardOut
PlanCardOut.description: The Wellness Plan card on the Home Dashboard and at the top of My Health.

PlanEdit.title: PlanEdit

PlanNew.title: PlanNew
PlanNew.description: 8.2's + Add plan. There's only one Free trial, so the type is Individual or Family.

PlansOut.title: PlansOut
PlansOut.description: Story 9.1's plan screen. Every price comes from one place (app/billing/catalog.py).

PreferenceIn.title: PreferenceIn
PreferenceIn.description:
One type's choice. With enabled true and neither push nor email, notices of this type
still appear in the notification centre.

PreferencesIn.title: PreferencesIn
PreferencesIn.description:
The types to change. Types left out keep their current choice, so the app can send one
row or the whole screen.

PreviewOut.title: PreviewOut
PreviewOut.description: 9.2's Preview: the version as clients will see it on the Policy Update screen.

ProductOut.title: ProductOut
ProductOut.description:
A product link or a link to a test Deborah has supplied (adults only). Links only: never
a price, discount, "buy now" or "Subscribe & Save".

ProfileDetails.title: ProfileDetails
ProfileDetails.description: A profile's details for View & edit (story 8.2).

ProfileEdit.title: ProfileEdit
ProfileEdit.description:
View & edit a family member (story 8.2). Send the fields to change; the app may also send
the whole form.

- A write-in can be sent on its own while the saved choice takes one.
- Changing the relationship needs the advocate consent again, in the same request (story
  2.2's step 4), so the consent always matches who the member is to the client.
- Date of birth and sex at birth are read-only: accepted unchanged, refused if different.

ProfileOptions.title: ProfileOptions
ProfileOptions.description:
The answer options for each intake question, and for View & edit (stories 2.1, 2.2,
8.2). The keys are the field names sent to PATCH /profiles/{id}/intake.

ProgressOut.title: ProgressOut
ProgressOut.description: The To Do list's progress, like a pill organiser: one dot per item, filled when done.

ProviderNotesOut.title: ProviderNotesOut
ProviderNotesOut.description: The notes screen (story 3.5): always the latest version.

PublicPolicyOut.title: PublicPolicyOut
PublicPolicyOut.description:
A published version's text, for the apps' policy screens (no sign-in needed: the
policies are public).

PushTokenIn.title: PushTokenIn
PushTokenIn.description:
The token the phone's push service gave the app. Send it after every sign-in, and again
when the service gives the app a new one.

RequestSupport.title: RequestSupport
RequestSupport.description:
Story 10.1: the client tapped Yes on the Oracle's offer to send something to the support
team (a `support_offer` card). `message_id` is the Oracle reply with the offer, and `kind`
the offer's `request_kind`: `knowledge_gap` (a question the Oracle couldn't answer) or
`talk_to_support` (the client asked for a person). The client message that reply answers
is what's sent. Safe to repeat: the same offer sends one request.

"Consult with support team" isn't sent here: its card opens 10.1's Consult form, which goes
to POST /profiles/{id}/support-requests with kind `consultation`.

ReviewBody.title: ReviewBody
ReviewBody.description:
Mark as reviewed (with any notes), or mark it Not yet reviewed again. Notes left out are
kept as they are.

SafetyAdviceOut.title: SafetyAdviceOut
SafetyAdviceOut.description:
What the safety check found in the message just sent (story 3.2), and the advice line
the backend added to the conversation for it, to show straight away.

SafetyHoldOut.title: SafetyHoldOut
SafetyHoldOut.description:
An open emergency or crisis hold (story 3.2): the conversation is paused, and no reply is
given, until the client picks one of the options (POST .../safety-choice). Messages sent
meanwhile are saved and checked, but get no reply.

SectionItemOut.title: SectionItemOut
SectionItemOut.description: One line of a section: a question, a test, a step, a product, a medication.

SendMessage.title: SendMessage
SendMessage.description:
A client message. The app makes `client_msg_id` (a UUID) once per message and sends it
again with any retry, so a message is never saved twice. Symptoms ticked in the symptom
check arrive as part of the text. A tapped answer sends its label as the text, and what
was tapped as `answer` (see Answer in app/oracle/contract.py).

`outside_us` is true when the device's location shows the client is outside the US (story
3.2): the safety advice then gives the local emergency number instead of 911 and 988. Leave
it out when the location is unknown, and the US numbers are shown.

SetupCodeSent.title: SetupCodeSent
SetupCodeSent.description:
The next screen is the Verification screen: a code was emailed to the invite's address
(Admin 1.1).

SignUpCheck.title: SignUpCheck
SignUpCheck.description:
The body of POST /auth/signup/check. Other sign-up fields the app sends with it (the
first name from step 1, say) are ignored, so the app can send the form as it stands.

StartSubscription.title: StartSubscription
StartSubscription.description:
Subscribe (9.1). The client confirms the monthly total they were shown (the plan plus
any add-ons) and the renewal disclaimer: a different total means the price changed.

SummaryCard.title: SummaryCard
SummaryCard.description: A summary in the profile's list (My Visit Notes, story 5.1).

SupportNotesBody.title: SupportNotesBody
SupportNotesBody.description: The team's internal notes, replaced as a whole (empty clears them).

SupportRequestBody.title: SupportRequestBody
SupportRequestBody.description:
The Contact support team form ("How can we help?", kind talk_to_support) or the Consult
with support team form ("What would you like help with?", kind consultation). The app makes
`client_request_id` (a UUID) once per request and sends it again with any retry, including
a request it kept while offline, so a request is never sent twice.

SupportRequestFromConversation.title: SupportRequestFromConversation
SupportRequestFromConversation.description: A request sent from the conversation (story 10.1).

SupportRequestSent.title: SupportRequestSent
SupportRequestSent.description: A request the team has received. `message` is the confirmation to show the client.

SupportRequestSummary.title: SupportRequestSummary
SupportRequestSummary.description: A row in the team's list.

TeenHealthConsentBody.title: TeenHealthConsentBody
TeenHealthConsentBody.description:
Story 12.2: the parent confirms the updated Health Consent, as medical advocate, for an
invited teen.

TeenInviteBody.title: TeenInviteBody
TeenInviteBody.description:
Story 1.5: the parent accepted the Teen account privacy disclaimer ("I understand &
continue") and typed the teen's email. Sent for the family draft whose Teen Profile Choice is
"own_account" (story 2.2).

TeenInviteOut.title: TeenInviteOut
TeenInviteOut.description:
What the teen setup screen shows (story 1.5): the email, filled in and locked, and the
first name the parent typed, to start the name field with.

TeenInviteToken.title: TeenInviteToken
TeenInviteToken.description: The token from the invite link's `#token=...`. Sent in the body, never in a URL.

TeenSignUpBody.title: TeenSignUpBody
TeenSignUpBody.description:
Story 1.5's Teen Account Setup: About You, then Create Password with the email locked.
No code, no consent and no subscription step: the parent gave consent and pays.

TeenSignedUp.title: TeenSignedUp
TeenSignedUp.description:
The teen's account is ready and this device is signed in. Next comes the teen onboarding
(story 2.3) on `profile_id`, with PATCH /profiles/{id}/intake, after the welcome.

TickItem.title: TickItem
TickItem.description: Tick a To Do item (done) or untick one ticked by mistake.

TrialBanner.title: TrialBanner
TrialBanner.description: Story 4.1's free trial banner, with a Choose a plan button (9.1's plans screen).

UpdateHealthProfileWidget.title: UpdateHealthProfileWidget
UpdateHealthProfileWidget.description:
Shown 3, 6 and 12 months after the health profile's last update, and after a logged
provider visit, until the profile is updated again.

UpgradePrompt.title: UpgradePrompt
UpgradePrompt.description:
The trial (or a subscription) has ended: the dashboard shows the upgrade prompt, and
every widget is locked. The codes are the ones the message box refuses with.

VerificationRequired.title: VerificationRequired
VerificationRequired.description: The next screen is the Verification screen: a code was emailed.

VersionRef.title: VersionRef
VersionRef.description: A published version in the history, which opens read-only.

VisitLogForm.title: VisitLogForm
VisitLogForm.description:
Log your visit, pre-filled (5.2). For notes: the specialty, provider name, visit date
(the appointment's), the reason and the requested labs, with the notes themselves to show
read-only. Standalone: only the first name and date of birth.

VisitLogIn.title: VisitLogIn
VisitLogIn.description:
Story 5.2's Log your visit form, which follows the Provider Visit Summary template.
Visit date, why you went and the specialty are mandatory; everything else is optional.
There's no upload. Sent whole on every save: an edit replaces the log's fields.

VisitLogOut.title: VisitLogOut
VisitLogOut.description: A logged visit (5.2). It stays in the app: there's no download.

VisitNoteCard.title: VisitNoteCard
VisitNoteCard.description:
One card in My Visit Notes. `type` says which screen it opens:

- guidance_summary: GET /conversations/{conversation_id}/guidance-summary (PDF there too);
- provider_notes: GET /provider-notes/{id}, with Edit appointment, Download PDF, Print and
  Copy text. Not logged yet: `can_log_visit` (Log visit). Logged: `visit_log_id`, with Ask
  the Oracle (`ask_prompt`) and Edit;
- visit_log: a standalone visit, GET /visit-logs/{id}, with Ask the Oracle and Edit. No
  download.

VisitNotesOut.title: VisitNotesOut
VisitNotesOut.description:
Upcoming appointments first, soonest first, then everything else, newest first.
`message` is 5.1's "No notes yet" (with a prompt to start a conversation) or "No search
results".

VisitNotesSearch.title: VisitNotesSearch
VisitNotesSearch.description:
Search by title, topic, specialty or provider name. Sent in the body, never the URL:
what someone searches for can be health information.

VisitNotesWidget.title: VisitNotesWidget
VisitNotesWidget.description: Quick access to My Visit Notes (5.1). Always shown.

VisitReviewOut.title: VisitReviewOut
VisitReviewOut.description:
What the Oracle made of the visit (5.2). `pending` until it's done, a few seconds after
a save; `failed` while it's being tried again.

WellnessPlanOut.title: WellnessPlanOut
WellnessPlanOut.description: The plan screen: always the latest version.

WellnessPlanScreen.title: WellnessPlanScreen
WellnessPlanScreen.description:
`plan` is null before the profile's first guidance summary, with 7.1's "No plan yet"
message.

WellnessPlanWidget.title: WellnessPlanWidget
WellnessPlanWidget.description:
Shown once the profile has a Wellness Plan; greyed out during the trial (7.1). View
plan opens GET /profiles/{profile_id}/wellness-plan.

WhatsNextWidget.title: WhatsNextWidget
WhatsNextWidget.description: One or two suggested next steps; shown when there are any (greyed out on the trial).

app__admin__clients__schemas__FamilyMemb.title: FamilyMemberOut
app__admin__clients__schemas__FamilyMemb.description: A managed family member: first name, relationship and age only.

app__billing__schemas__SubscriptionOut.title: SubscriptionOut
app__billing__schemas__SubscriptionOut.description: Story 11.3's current plan, and what the app needs around it.

app__profiles__schemas__FamilyMemberOut.title: FamilyMemberOut
app__profiles__schemas__FamilyMemberOut.description: A card on the Manage Family screen (story 8.2).

app__teens__schemas__InvitedTeenOut.title: InvitedTeenOut
app__teens__schemas__InvitedTeenOut.description:
An invited teen's card on Manage Family (story 8.2): their first name and relationship
as the parent entered them, and the status. Never the teen's health, profile or activity.
